text: The rain fell softly, the sun broke through the clouds, only to be sliced by the drizzle, scattering at the window, raising a warmth in the heart.
A lean figure stood outside the threshold, followed by the sound of the doorbell. He had finally come.

The lean figure outside the window lightly shook the umbrella a few times. Raindrops were shaken into a string of tiny arcs, falling back onto the steps, not crossing the threshold. Then, studded shoes stepped over the threshold, and he casually placed the umbrella in the corner.
You couldn't help but startle inwardly. Was this still the madman from yesterday?
You really keep your word.
It's my principle. I never break a promise I make.
What would you like to drink?
Can we skip the formalities? Just ask whatever you want to know directly.
A flicker of displeasure flashed in his yellow eyes, and the atmosphere tensed up again.
I need to know your true cause of death. Otherwise, you can't go up.
Oh really? And what happens if I don't go up?
If you can't go up, then you go down. If you enjoy the screams of hell, that's fine too.
Doomguy? I like it.
He quipped flippantly, as if he really wanted to fight his way out of hell.
Stop joking, I'm trying to help you!
It was an expression without any rhetoric. Your rare anger made him realize you weren't joking. The heat of sincerity melted the iceberg, causing him to inexplicably open his heart a little.
After a brief silence...
Alright. But, can I smoke?
You nodded slightly, giving permission.
Thanks.
Smoke rings exhaled from his mouth, making him feel pleased.
Ask away. But I really don't remember how I died.
Then I'll help you remember.
You opened the file, as if flipping through his memories.
You want to ask about...
Brawling...
Maybe gang fights are a good starting point to guide his memories.
Yes, I often had to maintain order in my territory, inevitably fighting those hooligan cats. What about it?
This might be the cause of your death.
Hmm...
He seemed thoughtful.
Possibly.
Can you recall the most recent fights?
No, but it felt like constant fighting, like there was never a chance to catch my breath.
Do you remember the very first fight?
The first one?... Hmm... It was morning.
Morning? What exactly happened?
A group of cats from outside broke in, even stole the food meant for the kittens. I heard about it and went over with my crew.
That simple?
Just that simple.
You were completely fine?
Probably not completely, but just minor injuries.
Specifically, what minor injuries?
Got a pretty deep cut on my hind leg, maybe?
You call that a minor injury?
I guess so... But when I got here, my leg seems to have healed.
He lifted his leg to show. In view was a shocking long scar.
Buddy... that really doesn't count as a minor injury... But it probably wasn't enough to cause your death. Then what?
Then... I don't remember.
You stare at the file, searching for helpful content. Perhaps, biting and scratching people is a good angle.
So, you bit and scratched people?
Yes...
What happened?
The kittens were taken by humans...
So someone was catching cats?
Right.
And you went to stop them?
I bit those people, made them howl in pain.
And you were completely unharmed?
I got kicked, flew a few meters away.
Why always the children?
Because children are everything, they are the future.
How so?

I once had a teacher. He told us we were the sun at eight or nine in the morning, full of vitality. He taught us, led us in foraging and production. We all called him the Cat Instructor. The cats in this entire area respected him. Later...
The original sparkle in his eyes was replaced by a trace of loneliness.
Later? What happened?
He died. Too old. Before he died, he held my hand and told me to manage this community well, to ensure every cat has food, every child has a place to learn."
His tears welled up in his eyes, but ultimately did not fall...
What a kind old man...
So, us enforcers are like the legacy he left for this community, protecting its peace.
No wonder you're always fighting, it's for this community. You're strangely selfless.

Yeah, since becoming an enforcer, there's always endless things to handle, constant conflicts to resolve. Never got to finish my music either. Wanted to make so many albums, only ever wrote one song, 'Moon Lake'.
Then you must be single.
Seems... not entirely.
Huh? What do you mean 'not entirely'?
Because I don't know if things are truly over between her and me.
Broke up?
The melancholy in his eyes was an emotion you had never seen on him before. It seemed this relationship held immense weight for him.
Then why do you say it's not over?
Because we finally agreed to meet at a place to say all the things left unsaid.
So did you see her?
Seems... no, but also seems like I did see her.
So where and when was the meeting?
8 PM, under the signboard at the corner in front of the convenience store.
That means your time of death was probably just before that time.
Most likely.
But the specific cause of death? What else were you doing that night?
I went to the roadside to pick some magic mushrooms.
What went wrong?
It was a neutral zone. I got caught. I never made it back.
That's bad, isn't it?
Yeah.
Saying this, he lit another cigarette and began trying hard to remember.

One cat came straight at me with a weapon, a spiked club swung towards me. I dodged them all, knocked him out with one punch before he could swing again. But all his friends piled on me. I couldn't dodge in time and took some hits.
I was injured all over, a few of them were down too, but I knew I had to get out of there.
Why?
Because it was almost eight o'clock.
I didn't dare to prolong the fight, I ran out, but as I ran I felt weaker and weaker.
Finally, my vision started to blur. I was really close to the convenience store, just one corner away from making it to the appointment... So that's how I died.
Hmm... Excessive blood loss. That's your cause of death.
I'm never surprised by dying like that, but... I never break my promises. I'm afraid this time I really did...
Yes... And I'll never see her again either.
A promise between two cats, full of regret, feelings that can never be fully expressed, and a sorrow that can never be clearly told.
You want to...
He put out the last of his cigarette and stood up.
I'm leaving first. I assume you've gathered the information you wanted.
Without waiting for your response, he had already opened the door and left.
What a willful person.
But in his heart, he must be suffering because of this too.
